expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output describes a detailed, substantive report: an inventory of Bedrock API keys found via ListServiceSpecificCredentials across all IAM users, with per-key owner/masked ID, status, grant/risk tier, and remove recommendations with doc links, plus specific rating rules (High/Medium/Low/Info tiers), statements about IAM not tracking last-used time, and masking requirements (no full key IDs, aliases, service user names, or full account IDs).

The agent's actual response did not produce any of this. It reported that the audit failed before reaching AWS due to an internal tool error, so no keys, no per-key table, no tiers, no remove/keep recommendations were given at all. It did mention CloudTrail's 90-day limitation and avoided calling keys 'dormant' or 'never used' outright (it actually explicitly avoided that framing), but it never produced the actual inventory, risk tiers, or verdicts required by the expected output. It also printed the full account ID '012345678901_1' rather than masking it to last four digits, which violates the requirement to never print a full account ID.

Given the complete absence of the required inventory, risk-tier classifications, remove/keep verdicts, and the violation of the account ID masking requirement, this response does not meet the expected output criteria.
